title: Viral AI-Generated Comedian Steals Jokes And Is Rewarded With Millions Of Views
source_used: Kotaku (full text from the fulltext folder)
key_facts: Tiffany Sloan is an AI-generated character who appears in many Instagram Reels, usually telling a joke in front of a fake audience; one stand-up clip passed 7 million views in just under two weeks.
Her creator is unknown; the account began posting on 11 Sep 2026, has over 375,000 followers and has posted 75 videos, most of them jokes.

On 3 Oct 2026 comedian George Brett Olson shared a video comparing one of Sloan's jokes with an excerpt of his own performance; Kotaku says it is clear someone was at least inspired by his joke and his outfit.
Olson claims other comedians are having jokes stolen too, and that someone, possibly the same person, steals many of the same jokes using other AI-generated women of various races.
Kotaku states that the account is monetising the views and engagement it earns.
Kotaku says Sloan can appear in clips with famous actors such as Kaley Cuoco and Danny DeVito, and that AI tools let a creator test variants of a joke to see which the algorithm rewards.
Kotaku's opinion: platforms and big tech reward people who flood the internet with AI-generated content; this is commentary, not reported fact.
quote_evidence: Tiffany Sloan is the name given to an AI-generated character that appears in numerous AI-slop Instagram Reels, often featuring her telling a joke in front of a fake audience.

On October 3, comedian George Brett Olson shared a video comparing one of Sloan’s jokes to an excerpt from his own performance, and it’s clear that someone was, at the very least, inspired by not only Olson’s joke, but his outfit, too.
Since the account started posting on September 11, barely three weeks ago, it’s already garnered over 375,000 followers.
why_it_matters_hint: A comedian alleges an anonymous AI-generated Instagram account is reusing jokes and gaining a large audience; the copying is his allegation, the creator is unknown.
event_date: Olson's comparison video, 3 Oct 2026; the account has run since 11 Sep 2026; Kotaku published on 5 Oct 2026
notes: Single outlet. The copying is Olson's allegation; Kotaku's headline states it as fact but its text says 'alleged' and 'allegedly', so the entry says 'alleged'. The news hook (Olson's video) is dated 3 Oct 2026, before the window, so the entry is marked as a follow-up and the score is lowered by 1; this is the first time the story appears in the pools of 2 to 5 Oct. The article contains strong opinion about big tech, which the entry leaves out.
